cells.tense: You are in the clearing with the pen already moving in your hand.
cells.act: sort the kinds of pull from one another
cells.ask: The pulls on you about a thing that is finishing — set them side by side and label each one: mine, borrowed, or just loud. Act on whichever turns out to be yours.
cells.core:
This is where a thing has to end for the next one to arrive, and naming what is finished comes naturally to you. Two or three readings of the situation can stay true at once; collapsing them into one verdict first is not required. You let them sit, and the line you draw comes out firmer for the wait. What you clear stays clear.

It takes a nerve of its own, not knowing everything you are ending. Knowing lands in you without argument, and it does not need the whole case built before you move. So take the pulls on you about something that is finishing and sort them by kind. Label each one honestly. Act on whichever turns out to be yours, and the ending will be further along than you thought.
cells.sheetLine: You can end a thing whole while more than one reading is still true.
cells.verb: declaring the shape of things and holding the line of it
cells.place: at the clearing where what is finished has to actually end

cells.tense: You will have cleared it before it has finished ending, and you are already braced for the next room.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Follow one ending you are inside of, from the comfortable answer down to the part of it that will not resolve, and stop there — do not surface into a plan.
cells.core:
You are at the clearing, and you are clearing faster than the thing can finish. An ending shows up and the next shape is already organized: drawn, named, the room rearranged around a structure that has not ended yet. From outside it reads as momentum. From inside it is a mind that will not let a thing complete, because completing it would mean standing in the depth of it with no answer ready.

Go into the one you are in. Not to fix the ending — to follow what it was until you reach the edge of what you know, the part that stays unresolved. Stay there instead of climbing back up to a plan. What you are braced against is that depth, and the depth is smaller than the brace. Meet it once, and what you claim next will be something that is actually there.

cells.tense: You are on the far side of a door that closed behind you, and the pen stayed down.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Today, do the next piece of whatever you are building or clearing. Then come back tomorrow and do the piece after that, until the work has grown past what you can hold in view at once.
cells.core:
The clearing is here and you are past a door that already closed, still facing it. Nothing got declared. What needed to end is half-open, and the shape of what comes next was not drawn, because the drawing stopped. Seeing it clearly is not the problem. The problem is that the pen stayed down, and the space around you has been arranged around something that is no longer true.

Skip the large declaration. Do the part you can do today. Whatever you are building or clearing, take the next piece of it now, the piece after that tomorrow. Craft does what nerve will not — steady work on the same thing until it grows past the size where you can see all of it at once. The ending takes care of itself once something is actually getting built. You only have to keep coming back to it.

cells.tense: You are clearing the ground and calling it something that happened on its own.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take something that ended this past year and put three things it gave you on paper — not the lesson, the yield — then read the list back to yourself as yours.
cells.core:
Things end around you and new shapes take their place, and your account of it is that you were present for the change. The endings get honored, the ground gets cleared, whatever comes next gets built, and none of that gets counted as yours. You will say the situation resolved itself, or the timing was right, or someone else made the call. The clearing has a hand in it, and that hand keeps its own name off the work.

Look at one ending from the past year and count what it produced. Not what you learned — the actual yield, what is in your life now because that thing finished. Put three of them on paper. Read the list back to yourself as yours, without adding a line about how it was probably just how things went. Naming the crop is how a person finds out they were farming. Nothing else has to change for that to land.

The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any image like 'broadcasting outward' or 'claiming territory' — cut.
